summary: Independent quality and security review passed. The immutable range contains exactly the expected one-commit change across the four allowed files. Required tests, syntax and travel checks, handback schema validation, evidence hash verification, exact candidate exercise, and base-revision RED reproduction all passed. No critical, high, or important introduced defect was found. Test coverage has a nonblocking gap for a few explicitly listed edge cases.

git.commit_subject: fix(git): make push ancestry scans merge-aware (33GOD-55)

evidence: git/hooks/_travels.py:405-417 verifies live destination and configured remote advertisements, validates each local tip, and subtracts reachable advertised commit ancestry.
git/hooks/_travels.py:437-460 scans each unpublished commit and uses combined merge diffs so inherited remote-known content is not rescanned while unpublished side parents are scanned independently.
The 25-test suite covers existing refs, new refs, multiple updates, octopus side parents, merge resolutions, stale tracking refs, missing advertised objects, branch deletion, and empty-root history.
The exact candidate exercise exited 0 and reported exactly one unpublished commit.
dimensions.assessment: Outgoing commit selection and merge-aware file and credential scanning are correct for the reviewed SHA-1 topology, including existing and new refs, multiple updates, merges, octopus parents, tags by implementation inspection, and stale or missing local remote objects.

evidence: git/hooks/_travels.py:373-392 rejects malformed stdin, invalid object identities, shallow repositories, replacement refs, and nonempty graft files.
git/hooks/_travels.py:405-410 requires the live advertised destination SHA to equal the exact pre-push old SHA.
All Git subprocesses used by push_scan now use check=True or explicit checked subprocess calls; failures propagate to the outer error path and produce exit 1.
Tests cover malformed stdin, incorrect advertised bases, unreadable and unreachable remotes, unfetchable objects, and stale unverified tracking refs.
dimensions.assessment: Malformed input, incomplete ancestry, failed Git commands, mismatched advertisements, and partial remote resolution fail closed rather than becoming clean results.

evidence: advertised_refs uses live ls-remote branch and tag identities rather than cached tracking refs.
resolve_remote_objects fetches only exact advertised object IDs into the disposable object store and dereferences annotated tags before treating them as commit ancestry.
The destination and every configured remote are enumerated; duplicate URLs are deduplicated by exact URL string.
Tests prove stale tracking refs cannot hide local work and missing live advertised objects are resolved without persistent ref mutation.
dimensions.assessment: Remote-known ancestry is based on live advertisements and exact object resolution. Configured remotes are deliberately part of the documented global trust set, and no local tracking ref can silently widen or replace that evidence.

evidence: git/hooks/_travels.py:399-403 creates a temporary object store with an alternates file and process-local GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY.
git/hooks/_travels.py:349-353 disables fetch-head, tags, submodules, auto-maintenance, ref mapping, and commit-graph writes for object resolution.
git/hooks/_travels.py:462-466 restores the prior GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY in finally; TemporaryDirectory cleanup covers ordinary exceptions and handled termination signals.

The fixture suite asserts refs, HEAD, branch, index, config, FETCH_HEAD, worktree, status, and temporary directory state are unchanged; the exact candidate snapshot was byte-identical before and after.
dimensions.assessment: The reviewed paths avoid persistent refs, FETCH_HEAD, index, worktree, and config mutation. Temporary fetched objects and environment state are cleaned on normal and handled failure paths.

evidence: Ordinary unpublished commit diffs are emitted to the existing guard scanner, preserving credential detection for values later removed.
Unpublished side parents are scanned independently, and novel merge-resolution additions are normalized before credential scanning.
Tests cover ordinary credentials, unpublished side-parent credentials removed by a merge, merge-resolution credentials, and inherited remote-known credential content without a false block.
The outer exception handler explicitly suppresses raw Git stderr and remote URLs, preventing credential-bearing command diagnostics from being printed.
dimensions.assessment: Credential detection remains fail-closed across ordinary commits, unpublished side parents, and merge resolutions while remote URLs and raw command stderr remain confidential.

evidence: All subprocess invocations use argv lists rather than shell interpolation.
Remote URLs and remote names are passed as arguments with -- separators where applicable; advertised ref names are never used as fetch destinations or refspec text.
Pre-push stdin is split into exactly four fields and local and remote object IDs are restricted to lowercase SHA-1 or SHA-256 hexadecimal forms.
The hook preserves original arguments, consumes stdin before chaining, propagates the local hook exit code, and never invokes a push or bypass option.
dimensions.assessment: The changed shell and Python boundaries use safe argv handling, strict identity validation, and preserved hook contract semantics. No command-injection or refspec-construction path was found.

evidence: Remote advertisements and exact-object resolution are performed once per distinct configured URL, with advertised object IDs deduplicated within each remote.
The implementation avoids command-line expansion of the known-commit set by feeding rev-list through stdin.
The exact candidate exercise completed successfully in the documented environment and reported one unpublished commit.
The design intentionally performs live remote enumeration and may transfer missing objects from every configured remote before allowing a push.
dimensions.assessment: The implementation preserves safety under large ancestry sets and duplicate remote data, but pre-push latency can grow with the number of configured remotes and stale object stores. The documented fail-closed behavior is preferable to weakening verification.

evidence: The Bash hook remains a thin wrapper around the Python helper and continues to source _guard.sh and chain the repository-local hook.
The helper retains direct _travels.py HEAD compatibility while adding a separate --push mode.
The shared sh() helper now checks command failures, matching the fail-closed requirement; callers are covered by the outer exception policy.
The exact candidate and local-hook tests verify argument, stdin, exit-code, and ordinary hook compatibility.
dimensions.assessment: The separation between Bash and Python is clear, exception behavior is explicit, direct helper compatibility is retained, and the implementation documents its ancestry and cleanup invariants.

evidence: git/tests/test_pre_push.py contains 25 deterministic tests using disposable local repositories and invokes the real reviewed pre-push hook boundary.
The independent base-revision reproduction caused both clean-merge tests to fail for the original false-positive ancestry scan, while the reviewed head passes them.
The suite covers negative security cases, credentials, malformed input, multiple updates, octopus topology, object fetching, cleanup, and local-hook chaining.

No focused regression test directly exercises SHA-256 repositories, annotated tag push advertisements, SIGTERM interruption during fetch, or preservation of a pre-existing custom GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY.
dimensions.assessment: The tests are discriminating and reproduce the original RED behavior, but the explicitly requested SHA-256, non-commit-tag, signal, and custom-object-store cases remain coverage gaps rather than observed implementation failures.

evidence: git/README.md documents live destination and configured-remote advertisement checks, exact advertised SHA matching, temporary object fetching, cleanup, fail-closed behavior, and the consumed-stdin/local-hook contract.
The documentation explains merge-aware ancestry subtraction, unpublished side-parent scanning, credential handling, and deletion behavior.
The documented escape hatch is clearly labeled as exceptional and does not alter the implementation's default fail-closed behavior.
The documented command suite matches the reviewed helper and hook interfaces.
dimensions.assessment: Operational behavior, failure modes, remote access requirements, cleanup expectations, commands, and escape-hatch semantics are accurately documented without encouraging routine bypass.

tests.summary: 25 tests ran and passed, including merge topology, fail-closed remote verification, credential scanning, cleanup, multi-update handling, and local-hook chaining.
Python helper and tests compiled successfully.
Both Bash hook files parsed successfully.

The immutable range has no whitespace errors.

findings.description: The focused regression suite does not directly cover SHA-256 repositories, annotated tag advertisements, SIGTERM interruption during an active fetch, or preservation of a caller-provided custom GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY/alternate object store.
findings.impact: Future regressions in these explicitly supported or security-sensitive edge cases could go undetected even though the reviewed implementation handles the primary SHA-1 merge topology correctly.
findings.evidence: git/tests/test_pre_push.py contains 25 tests covering SHA-1 fixtures, branch refs, merge and octopus topology, credentials, malformed input, and cleanup assertions, but no SHA-256, annotated-tag, signal, or custom-object-store fixture.
